source.title: A Theoretical Framework for Grokking: Interpolation followed by Riemannian Norm Minimisation
source.authors: Etienne Boursier; Scott Pesme; Radu-Alexandru Dragomir

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports grokking-like delayed generalization in new synthetic regression and matrix-completion settings, and tests a weight-decay/norm-minimization account there. It does not reproduce the modular-arithmetic experiments.
record.gate_note: The study's own results include theoretical results on regularized gradient flow and reported empirical loss and norm trajectories. It does not measure circuit formation, memorizing-component removal, training-set-size dependence, or grokking in LLMs. Initialization-scale comments are not a controlled comparison. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study's own experiments on matrix completion, a two-layer ReLU net and a diagonal linear net show delayed test improvement after training loss reaches zero. That is grokking-like delay on non-algorithmic synthetic regression data (V3). Weight norm falls as test loss improves, and a theory shows weight decay drives slow norm minimisation on the interpolation manifold (V5). No modular-arithmetic or other algorithmic task is run, so V1 is not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Two additions: the authors also argue the transition is not sudden, unfolding over time of order 1/λ. They also restrict the theory to regression with bounded dynamics, excluding classification, and leave extension to future work.
record.recipe_differences: Unlike the cited modular-addition transformer experiments, this paper develops an asymptotic gradient-flow theory and reports experiments on matrix completion and synthetic regression tasks, including ReLU and diagonal linear networks.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper argues that the initialisation scale affects whether a substantial second phase occurs: small-scale initialisation may leave little norm reduction to do, while large-scale initialisation can produce substantial drift. This is discussion, not a controlled sweep. It also gives a heuristic that grokking-like behavior is expected when λ is sufficiently small relative to the initial-gradient-to-solution-norm ratio.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors argue the grokking drop is not sudden. It unfolds over time of order 1/λ, comparable to the plateau, and looks abrupt only on log-scale plots (Sec. 4.2). This is theoretical, with no row.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The apparent suddenness of grokking is an artifact of log-time plotting; in linear time the transition lasts as long as the plateau.

fits_no_version.finding: In matrix completion, spurious singular values decay to zero while three approach the true values during the delayed phase. This is a continuous measure tracking the transition, but not a circuit in V2's sense.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Continuous structural measures (spectrum, norm) track the delayed-generalisation phase in non-algorithmic models.

record.problems: The theory requires bounded unregularized flow and a smooth stationary manifold, and is derived in the asymptotic regime λ → 0. The paper notes that its theory does not guarantee test improvement without additional generalization assumptions; its empirical examples are described qualitatively, with no uncertainty estimates. The ReLU example is outside the stated smooth theoretical framework, and the diagonal-network and matrix examples have manifold/singularity limitations discussed by the authors.

untested.parts: All of it. No algorithmic datasets, no accuracy from chance to near-perfect, no training-set-size dependence of the delay.
No circuit identification, memorising-component tracking, or circuit progress measures.
No images, text or molecules. Switching grokking on or off via initialisation scale or weight norm is only discussed (Sec. 4.2, footnote 5), not swept.
No critical dataset size and no ungrokking below it. No explicit comparison of the efficiency of a memorising versus a generalising circuit.
Not tested. Optimizer and floating-point artifacts are not examined.

missing.what: Heuristic condition for grokking: λ ≪ ||∇F(w0)||/||wGF||. Also the argument that small initialisation leaves no second phase (and footnote 5: same solution reachable without weight decay via small init). Discussion only.
missing.locator: Section 4.2 'Role of initialisation scale'; Appendix E; footnote 5

missing.what: Linear regression example with an explicit closed-form two-timescale trajectory toward the minimum-norm solution.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked the delay rows to V1, but none of the tasks is algorithmic, so they are relinked to V3. The V3 verdict covers only the 'non-algorithmic data' clause: the initialisation-scale switch is only argued. Theory needs smooth losses and the Morse-Bott property. The ReLU example lies outside it, and the matrix and diagonal-network cases hold only locally away from singular points. No error bars or seeds are reported. The study is not one of the original sources.

versions.untested_parts: The reported tasks are synthetic regression and matrix completion, not small algorithmic datasets such as modular arithmetic. The paper does not test chance-level test accuracy, training accuracy, or whether delay grows as the training set shrinks.
The paper does not identify or track a generalizing circuit, memorizing components, or circuit-specific progress measures.
No comparison tests grokking on images, text, or molecules, or switches grokking on and off through initialization scale or weight norm.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is studied.

The paper studies weight-decay-driven norm reduction and reports generalization improvements in its examples, but does not test whether a more efficient generalizing circuit displaces memorization, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking below that size.
The paper does not compare identifiable algorithms learned across runs.
The paper does not test adaptive-optimizer instabilities, softmax floating-point limits, or whether controlling numerical or optimizer choices removes grokking.

rows.measure: Trajectory dynamics and constrained ℓ2-norm minimization
rows.baseline: unregularized gradient flow converging to a stationary point of F
rows.value: The fast phase approaches the unregularized flow; on the rescaled slow timescale the trajectory follows Riemannian gradient flow minimizing the squared ℓ2 norm on the stationary manifold.

relation.reason: The study supplies its own theoretical results and experiments bearing on delayed generalization and weight-decay-driven norm reduction.

tranche.reason: Own experiments establish delayed test-loss improvement in synthetic regression and matrix completion, extending the setting beyond modular algorithmic tasks.

source_check.notes: Figure times are rescaled training time t_k=γk, not gradient-step counts; the ReLU prose and Figure 3 disagree on t3. The smooth bounded-flow theory excludes ReLU architectures and separable classification; experimental agreement does not remove those assumptions.

statements.correction: Figure 2 includes an unregularized λ=0 comparator; Section 5 compares regularized training with unregularized-flow solutions. Under Assumptions 1–2, the λ→0 slow dynamics follow constrained Riemannian norm reduction. This optimization result alone does not imply improved test loss. No capability check is stated.
statements.problem: The slow-manifold theory is described correctly, but the assertion that this study reports no controls overlooks its unregularized comparator.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: matrix-completion, two-layer ReLU, and diagonal-linear synthetic examples
reader_labels.reason: The reported trajectories show training loss reaching zero or nearly zero before test performance improves later (r2–r3, r5–r6, r8–r9). These examples support delayed generalization in the studied synthetic settings, but do not test the stated algorithmic-data or training-set-size conditions.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: theoretical analysis and the three reported synthetic examples
reader_labels.reason: The analysis derives slow norm minimization on the stationary manifold, and the empirical examples associate later norm reduction with improved generalization or lower-complexity solutions (r1, r3–r4, r6–r7, r9–r10). The paper does not test the critical-dataset-size or ungrokking predictions.
